move: light cuts the diagonal, before halves slide apart to reveal the after
how: The before image is split into two triangular clip-path halves over the after layer. Before creeps from scale 1.08 to 1.0 and after from 1.0 to 1.1 linearly across D. A Before label slides in, then at 0.18D a bright edge line draws along the diagonal (scaleX 0→1, expo.inOut); at 0.27D the two halves slide apart perpendicular to the cut (x/y ±1000 along the diagonal normal, expo.inOut 1.1s) as the edge fades and widens. The After label slides in and a big word rises from a mask at 0.44D, exits up at 0.78D; at 0.85D the halves return with expo.inOut, the edge blinks, and the Before label returns to close the loop.
adapt: Swap the image and the before/after filters, the labels and the big word; the diagonal is computed from 1280x720 so recompute ang for another aspect. Keep the 0.5s edge draw and 1.1s expo.inOut split.
port: mount(el, shot) builds .layer.after and two .layer.before.half elements with polygon clip-paths, .edge, labels and .big; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline computing nx/ny from el's aspect and offsets as fractions of D (edge 0.9/5, split 1.35/5, return 4.25/5). Scope selectors to el.
caveats: the diagonal normal is hard-coded from 1280x720
filters on three full-frame image layers
the edge line is positioned by CSS for the 1280x720 diagonal
